QuantRule glossary
==================

Precise terms used by the shell and the contracts.

NDJSON
  Newline-delimited JSON: one JSON value per line, oldest first for candles and timeframes.

report bundle
  One engine's directory under a lab result folder. It holds report.json, summary.txt,
  provenance.json, and the engine's artifacts.

data version
  The caller-supplied identity of an input series: source, timeframe, and coverage. The engine
  records it and never infers it from the path.

lab result folder
  data/lab-result-YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ in UTC. It holds the five report bundles and the root
  summary.txt.

timeframe ladder
  The configured 1m/5m/15m/1h series. Each timeframe is first-class; M1 is the source and
  M5/M15/H1 are derived by the data engine.

M1 source
  A CSV whose rows are one minute apart. A ladder consumer rejects a file whose rows are never
  closer than a coarser timeframe instead of labeling it 1m; the error names the observed
  cadence.

Direction
  A continuous [-1,+1] score of EMA alignment. Positive is bullish, negative is bearish, and
  zero is neutral alignment, not missing data.

Momentum
  A continuous [-1,+1] force from RSI, with acceleration and intensification. It is not a
  confidence score.

Structure
  The confirmed swing sequence and EMA levels: a discrete swing code and a signed score. It is
  not another trend-strength score.

Progression
  A leg's unclamped progress and ordinal stage toward its target. It is not a probability or a
  forecast of reversal.

axis resolution
  One axis's continuous value, ordinal bucket, and unavailable reason for one timeframe and bar.

consensus
  A per-timeframe count of bullish, bearish, and neutral axis votes, with the weakest axis.
  Progression does not vote and the count is not an average.

cross-axis agreement
  A count over Direction, Momentum, and Structure. It is never averaged into a single score.

level event
  Price interacts with an EMA or confirmed swing level. Subtypes are test/retest, cross, and
  break; break precedes cross, which precedes test.

divergence event
  Price swings and RSI disagree directionally: regular or hidden, bullish or bearish. It is
  emitted only after the newer pivot is confirmed.

signal event
  A discrete change in a reading: an RSI threshold crossing, an EMA crossover, or a compact
  state change. It is not a vote.

occurrence bar
  The bar on which the underlying relationship occurred.

availability bar
  The first closed bar on which the model could know the measurement. An event never reaches an
  earlier bar.

confirmed pivot
  A swing extreme confirmed after k bars on both sides: 2 for minor, 5 for major. It records
  both occurrence and availability.

leg
  A movement from a pivot origin toward a target, maintained separately at the minor and major
  scales per timeframe.

progression stage
  The ordinal stage of a leg. It is null while the origin is unconfirmed or the target is
  unstable.

Layer 1
  The research layer with the candle, readings, axis metrics, context, and consensus for every
  ladder bar.

Layer 2
  The research layer with each axis's continuous value, ordinal bucket, and unavailable reason.

Layer 3
  The research layer with the as-of higher-timeframe block and the cross-timeframe aggregates.

provenance
  The provenance.json record of a bundle's data version, periods, config files, resolved values,
  and artifacts.

in-sample
  Data used to form or tune a hypothesis. A result on this data alone is not validation.

out-of-sample
  Data not used to form or tune a hypothesis. It is required before a result is called
  promising.

walk-forward
  Adjacent in-sample and out-of-sample windows evaluated in sequence.

input cap
  The maximum M1 candles a command accepts. An over-cap input fails and is never silently
  truncated.

deterministic
  The same input and configuration produce the same bytes. No clock, unseeded randomness, or
  unordered iteration affects the result.
